# loading data
```{r}
data<-read.csv("diabetes.csv")
head(data)
```

# general linear models(GLM)
## logistic regression
- is a type of regression analysis used for prediction of outcome of a categorical dependant variable based on one or more predictor variables.
- it is used when the dependant variable is binary(0/1. yes/ no, true /false)
- it estimates the probability of the dependant variable being 1(or less) given the values of the independent variables
- The logistic function is used to model the relationship between the dependant and independent variables.
- the logistic function is defined as:


# omit missing values
```{r}
omit_miss<-na.omit(data)
head(omit_miss)
```

## check columns name
```{r}
names(data)
```
### convert variables to factor from integer and from character
```{r}
data$diabetes<-factor(data$diabetes,
                      levels=c(0,1),
                      labels=c("No", "Yes"))
data$hypertension<-factor(data$hypertension,
                          levels=c(0,1),
                      labels=c("No", "Yes") )
data$heart_disease<-factor(data$heart_disease,
                          levels=c(0,1),
                      labels=c("No", "Yes") )
data$smoking_history<-factor(data$smoking_history)

```

# confirm for missing values
```{r}
colSums(is.na(data))
```

### check the frequency of diabetes case
```{r}

frq(data, diabetes)
```

#### visualize the frequency of diabates cases
```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(
  x=diabetes, fill=diabetes
))+
  geom_bar(alpha=0.7)+
  labs(
    title="Bar plot of diabetes outcome",
    x="Diabetes",
    y="count"
    
  )+
  theme_classic()
```



### partition the dataset into training and testing sets 
```{r}
set.seed(123)
trainIndex<-createDataPartition(data$diabetes,p=.8,
                                list=FALSE,
                                times=1)
train<-data[trainIndex, ]
test<-data[-trainIndex, ]

```

### check the dimension of training and testing set
```{r}
dim(train)
dim(test)
```

### set the reference categories
```{r}
data$smoking_history<-relevel(data$smoking_history, ref="current")
data$hypertension<-relevel(data$hypertension, ref="No")
data$heart_disease<-relevel(data$heart_disease, ref="No")
```

### fit a logistic regressin model
```{r}
model<-glm(diabetes~., data=train, family=binomial)
summary(model)
```

### Re-estimate the glm model by specifying the reference category for categorical variables
```{r}
model1<-glm(diabetes~age+hypertension+heart_disease+
              smoking_history+BMI+
              HbA1c_level+ blood_glucose_level,
            data=train, family=binomial)
summary(model1)
```

# interpretation **
-  unit in (positive integer Estimate) increases the probability of someone being diabetic
 - unit in (negative integer Estimate) decreases the probability of someone being diabetic


## report
```{r}
report(model1)
```

## model predictions
```{r}
probabilities<-predict(model1, newdata=test, type="response")
head(probabilities)
```


## convert the probabilities to factors 'Yes' and 'No'
```{r}
predicted_class<-ifelse(probabilities>0.5, "yes", "no")
predict_factor<-factor(predicted_class, levels=levels(test$diabetes))
head(predicted_class)
```

## confusion matrix
```{r}
lg_cm<-confusionMatrix(predict_factor, reference=test$diabetes, positive="Yes")
lg_cm
```

## four fold confusion matrix plot
```{r}
m<-lg_cm$byClass[c(1,2,5,7,11)]
m
```

## plotting confusion matrix plot
```{r}
fourfoldplot(lg_cm$table, col=c(2,3), main="confusion matrix for logistic regression model")
```
